walkthroughs.body_html: Two suspects each face the choice to confess or stay silent. Confessing is a dominant strategy - but if both confess, both serve long sentences. Mutual silence would be better.
Named after John Nash, the equilibrium is the point where no single player wants to switch strategy. In the prisoner's dilemma, the Nash outcome is (Confess, Confess).
Real firms face the same logic on price-cutting, advertising or pollution. Repeated games and communication can shift outcomes toward cooperation - or to tacit collusion.
